stack.frontend: Simple responsive web app (React/Next.js) for merchant dashboard + optional WhatsApp-based invoice creation flow
stack.backend: Node.js or Python (FastAPI) service handling UBL 2.1 XML generation, cryptographic stamping (ECDSA), and ZATCA API calls
stack.database: Postgres (e.g. Supabase) storing merchant profiles, invoices and the mandatory 6-year archive
stack.authentication: Simple email/OTP or Supabase auth for merchant login; no Nafath required for MVP
stack.ai: Optional: LLM (Claude/GPT) to help merchants convert free-text/voice item lists into structured invoice line items via WhatsApp chat
stack.apis: ZATCA Fatoora API — self-service Compliance CSID -> Production CSID flow, sandbox at sandbox.zatca.gov.sa, confirmed NOT to require an accredited/certified provider status (any taxpayer/solution meeting technical requirements is compliant)
stack.hosting: Small VPS or serverless (Vercel/Render) + Supabase; consider GCC-region hosting (e.g. AWS me-south-1 Bahrain) for data-residency comfort given 6-year tax-record retention
stack.payments: Moyasar — flat 2.5% per transaction, no monthly/setup fee, Mada settlement T+1 (per search snippet, GulfSaasReview/logiolegion comparison)
stack.integrations: Optional WhatsApp Cloud API via a BSP (360dialog/Twilio/Wati) for chat-based invoice creation; Meta per-message pricing ~SAR 0.04 (utility) to ~SAR 0.19 (marketing) plus BSP markup/monthly fee (per cached search result)

mvp_scope: Merchant onboarding + Production CSID registration via ZATCA sandbox then production API
Simple invoice creation form (or WhatsApp chat) generating ZATCA-compliant XML + QR
Submission to ZATCA reporting/clearance API and storage of the signed archive
Basic invoice list/dashboard + PDF/QR export for the customer copy
Moyasar-billed monthly subscription for the merchant
results.monthly_run_cost_sar: ≈150-400 SAR (hosting/DB + optional WhatsApp BSP fees; scales with invoice volume; Moyasar has no fixed monthly fee, only the 2.5% transaction cut)

regulatory.requirement: ZATCA e-invoicing (Fatoora) Phase 2 mandatory integration for all VAT-registered businesses; Wave 24 lowers threshold to SAR 375,000 turnover, deadline 30 Jun 2026

No formal accreditation/licence is legally required to build a ZATCA-compliant solution — self-integration via Compliance CSID/Production CSID is explicitly valid; ZATCA's own Solution Providers Directory is optional, not mandatory
PDPL applies to any customer/invoice personal data stored (names, amounts, contact info); requires processing records, security and cross-border transfer safeguards
Freelance certificate (free, MHRSD) is sufficient to operate solo without hiring; a Commercial Registration (~SAR 1,200-2,000/yr) becomes advisable once selling B2B SaaS contracts at scale

data_dependencies: ZATCA Fatoora sandbox/production API — publicly documented and self-serve, confirmed available
Each merchant's own CR/VAT number (their data, not a founder dependency)
blockers: High liability exposure: fines are SAR 5,000-50,000 per violation, so any bug in XML/cryptographic-stamp generation directly costs the customer money — support and correctness burden is heavier than a typical CRUD SaaS

Crowded, well-funded incumbent field (Qoyod, Wafeq, Fatora.io, Daftra, Rewaa) already ZATCA-compliant with brand trust; a solo-built tool must win purely on price/simplicity for the very smallest merchants
Government-mandated cryptographic/XML spec correctness requires careful engineering and thorough sandbox testing before going live — not a quick weekend build despite no licensing barrier
results.summary: Technically feasible solo: ZATCA explicitly allows self-integration without an accredited-provider licence (confirmed via search of ZATCA's own Solution Providers Directory page and developer guides), and Moyasar gives a simple, cheap KSA payment rail. The real risk is not regulatory access but competitive crowding and liability — a bug in tax-invoice generation directly exposes the customer to real fines, so QA/sandbox testing time should not be underestimated.

data_dependencies: No confirmed public Qiwa or GOSI API for a solo/independent developer — this is a genuine unknown, not just an unverified detail

blockers: No evidence of self-serve Qiwa/GOSI developer API access; only large EOR/payroll firms (Mercans, Origami) appear to have integration relationships, likely via commercial partnership rather than open signup — without this, the tool cannot auto-sync data and reduces to a manual-entry calculator, undermining the 'reduces duplicate entry' value proposition

Legal-accuracy liability: an incorrect quota calculation could lead a customer to make a wrong compliance decision (risking Red-tier status) — significant support/liability burden for a solo operator maintaining a 269-role rules table by hand
Real demand is unquantified — only qualitative complaint/guide evidence found, no confirmed count of SMEs near Red tier or willingness-to-pay data
results.summary: Buildable as a manual-entry compliance calculator (EASY-MODERATE tech), but the core value proposition (eliminating duplicate portal work) depends on Qiwa/GOSI data access that could not be confirmed as available to an independent solo developer in this session. Without live sync, this becomes a rules-table app competing against free spreadsheets and paid HR consultancies — feasible to build, uncertain to differentiate or monetize.
